title: Beyond Access: Guided LLM Scaffolding for Independent Learning in Undergraduate Statistics
abstract: arXiv:2606.01375v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly entering students' learning practices, but their educational value may depend on whether they are used to support reasoning or to complete tasks without engaging in the underlying reasoning. This study examines guided LLM use in an undergraduate Probability and Statistics course, focusing on the distinction between assigned LLM access and the quality of students' actual interaction with the model. In a four-week quasi-experimental summer program, students were organized into three balanced conditions: no LLM access, unrestricted LLM access, and guided LLM access. The guided condition used the same LLM platform as the unrestricted condition, but students received explicit training and rules intended to promote reasoning-focused help-seeking, stepwise hints, verification, and ethical use. translated_title: 超越访问：引导式大语言模型支架在本科统计学独立学习中的应用
translated_abstract: arXiv:2606.01375v3 公告类型：替换-交叉 摘要：大语言模型（LLMs）正日益进入学生的学习实践，但其教育价值可能取决于它们是被用于支持推理，还是在不参与底层推理的情况下完成任务。本研究考察了在本科概率与统计课程中引导式LLM的使用，重点关注分配LLM访问权限与学生实际与模型互动质量之间的区别。在一项为期四周的准实验暑期项目中，学生被分为三个平衡条件：无LLM访问、无限制LLM访问和引导式LLM访问。引导条件使用与无限制条件相同的LLM平台，但学生接受了明确的培训和规则，旨在促进以推理为导向的求助、逐步提示、验证和道德使用。所有测验和延迟的期末考试均在无LLM或外部辅助的情况下完成，从而能够评估学习成果。
tldr: 该研究通过对比无访问、无限制访问和引导式访问三种条件，发现引导式LLM使用能显著提升本科统计学学生的独立学习效果，强调访问质量而非单纯访问权限是关键。
en_tdlr: This study compares no, unrestricted, and guided LLM access in undergraduate statistics, finding that guided scaffolding enhances independent learning outcomes, emphasizing interaction quality over mere access.
